kind.rationale: One bridge instance per destination network (design section 1.2); the frontend selects the actor (section 1.5).

standard.rationale: foundry/src/BridgedIcUSD.sol (escrow-backed ERC-20, 8 decimals) deploys unchanged on this chain per the EVM facts file; D5 (settled for planning) reuses identical bytecode.

signed_payload.value: EIP-1559 (type 2) transaction signing hash with EIP-155 chain-id rules (v = {0,1} + CHAIN_ID*2 + 35 for legacy envelopes); the threshold secp256k1 output is directly usable.

value.text: HYPE for the minter, admin and deployer addresses; a plain EOA must first receive HYPE on HyperEVM.
Only if deployment needs a big block: the sender must be an existing HyperCore user and enable big blocks (usingBigBlocks).

open_decisions.topic: Generalize the Base Wasm in place or build a separate EVM artifact

choice.rationale: Design section 12 (settled for planning): in-place source generalization on a working branch, Base behavior and stable state preserved; no deployed Base canister is upgraded; the EVM stack is not copied into a second artifact.

open_decisions.topic: Candid method names when the EVM Wasm is generalized in place

choice.rationale: Design section 12 (settled for planning): new EVM instances keep the legacy Base-named Candid methods and fields at first, documented, routed by the per-network actor; generic aliases are optional later.

open_decisions.topic: RPC service variants for new EVM networks

choice.rationale: Design section 12 (settled for planning): additive native RPC-service variants where useful. The absence of a published endpoint list does not prove Custom impossible or force this API change; the provider and finality requirements still apply.

open_decisions.topic: Quorum for chains that publish one keyless public endpoint

choice.rationale: Design section 12 (raised by BB-34, still a recommendation): a quorum may need keyed providers, which conflicts with keeping no secrets in canister state. Use keyless independent providers only until a reviewed key-handling design exists; otherwise the chain stays disabled.

open_decisions.topic: Non-Base EVM contracts: identical bytecode or a relabeled, newly reviewed contract

choice.rationale: Design section 12 (settled for planning): reuse identical BridgedIcUSD bytecode, keeping CONTRACT_VERSION and its Base-labelled bridge-out domain; chain id and contract stay in the id preimages; only new off-chain instance domains are chain-qualified, and Base reproduces its strings exactly.

open_decisions.topic: Testnet escrow: real icUSD ledger or a test ledger

choice.rationale: Design section 12 (settled for planning): synthetic test ledgers for future testnet demos; no real canonical icUSD is locked for a new testnet rollout under this groundwork.

activation_blockers.text: The Base Wasm accepts only the Base chain ids and the BaseMainnet provider variant. The chain allow-list, provider mapping, domain slug and deploy-script allow-list need a reviewed change before this destination can be installed (D1, settled for planning as in-place generalization).

The official default JSON-RPC serves eth_call against the latest block only, not a numbered finalized block, but the observer needs numbered finalized contract state. Needs archive-capable independent providers, or a reviewed observer redesign that does not need historical state. Not config-only.
Only one official public endpoint was found for this network. A quorum of 2 independent providers needs more, and keyed provider URLs conflict with the no-secrets-in-state rule.
The docs say the EVM is secured by HyperBFT but state no finality or reorg behavior and no support for the safe or finalized tags.
Estimated deploy gas on Base (about 2.8M) sits close to the 3M small-block limit. If deployment needs a big block, the sender must be an existing HyperCore user and enable big blocks.
Each address may queue only the next 8 nonces and transactions older than 1 day are pruned, so the nonce lane must respect that queue.
The controller and upgrade-authority model for this instance and its chain-side authorities is not decided (D6). The controller set is the root of trust for escrow and every signature.

value.typical_wait: about 1 second small blocks and 1 minute big blocks; EVM finality and tag semantics are not stated in a primary source, so the required finalized tag is recorded but not claimed to work

min_quorum.rationale: Baseline from the Base bridge design (section 7.7): identical results from 2 of 3 independent providers. The EVM RPC canister skill recommends Threshold with total 3 and min 2.

outcall_notes.value: Not a native variant (Custom with the chain id). The default RPC limits eth_getLogs to 4 topics and 50 blocks, serves eth_call and state reads for the latest block only, and has no historical state.
